$schema_note: Skill-owned judgement only: which module provides which WORKFLOW option, the job that proves an option is active, and when a module applies. Job lists, stage order and module descriptions are NOT restated here -- they live in the library's own README.md, which is re-read every run.

shared_options.build: Satisfied by any language module (nodejs/python/golang/java), so it maps to no single provider.
shared_options.deploy: Satisfied by either GitOps module; withheld until `platform ship` wires a real DEPLOY_TARGET.

readme/.migration-guide.gitlab.yml.include_when: the repo publishes a versioned contract others pin. NOT a default: Migration:Check Existence is allow_failure:false, so it blocks every release of an application nobody upgrades against.

default_include_set.$note: Start here for a service repository and subtract with a stated reason. The common defect is an under-declared include list, which silently drops quality and supply-chain coverage while looking tidy.

required_variables.PROJECT_CACHE_KEY: Always declared, even though common/ defaults it to "". Value is the plain language name -- node, python, go, java -- not the project name or a version. It prefixes every cache key in the repo and sonarqube/ builds sonar-${PROJECT_CACHE_KEY}.
